sid_items_OXAGear_ArmorII_description: Para-aramid armor panels - Substantial ballistic protection, able to withstand hits from smaller caliber firearms. Dozens of layers of para-aramid fabric prevent bullet penetration and disperse the associated kinetic energy. Whilst lacking the protection offered by more substantial armor, it is significantly lighter and provides a level of flexibility that is unattainable with more durable plating.
sid_items_OXAGear_ArmorIII_description: UHMWPE armor plates - Formidable ballistic protection, able to withstand multiple hits from most assault rifles. Comprised of multiple sheets of ultra-high molecular weight polyethylene fused into rigid plates via hydraulic press. UHMWPE provides a higher level of protection than steel whilst remaining substantially lighter. It is also superior in preventing spalling; whilst steel plates can cause rounds to disintegrate into dangerous shrapnel, UHMWPE absorbs these fragments and prevents secondary injury.
sid_items_OXAGear_ArmorIV_description: Ceramic armor plates - Advanced ballistic prevention, rated to withstand armor-piercing rounds. Projectile penetration is prevented by a network of extremely hard ceramic tiles, and a UHMWPE backing layer disperses the energy of the projectile and limits the impact of blunt force trauma. It's superior performance comes at a cost; these incredibly durable panels are around 1 inch thick, rendering them completely inflexible and amounting to a substantial weight.
sid_items_OXAGear_LiningCE_description: A collection of chemically resistant elastomer inserts which provide protection against both electrical and chemical hazards. Whilst relatively flexible, they offer little in terms of breathability; an over-exerted wearer will soon find themselves struggling due with the accumulated heat.
sid_items_OXAGear_LiningTE_description: With a core of vermiculite fiberglass fabric, this durable lining provides exceptional thermal protection. The external coating was originally included for the reflection of radiant heat, but once it found its way into the hands of stalkers it was soon discovered to function as a makeshift Faraday cage, providing a safe path for electrostatic discharge. Despite its benefits, many find such an insulating material to be a hindrance under sustained exertion.
sid_items_OXAGear_LiningRad_description: A thin, metallic material designed to inhibit the passage of radioactive particles. It sacrifices some level of protection in exchange for remaining flexible and lightweight.
sid_items_OXAGear_DumpPouch_description: A large pouch for the rapid deposition of spent magazines, reducing the total time required to reload. A mesh base prevents the accumulation of dirt and moisture, and elasticated straps prevent the contents from rattling.
sid_items_OXAGear_AmmoPouch_description: Secure storage for magazines of various sizes. Comprised of a double layer of 500D Cordura, retention is ensured with adjustable side panels and securing bungee strap. This organised system of ammo storage facilitates rapid reloads, and the improved weight distribution reduces fatigue when travelling long distances.
sid_items_OXAGear_Boots_description: A pair of sturdy yet lightweight combat boots, designed for prolonged excursions.
sid_items_OXAGear_HydrationBasic_descrip: Comprised of a refillable bladder and flexible drinking tube, this hydration pack provides a simple but effective way of ensuring stalkers maintain an adequate fluid intake whilst on the move.
sid_items_OXAGear_HydrationAdv_descripti: A somewhat over-engineered hydration pack; with the bladder held close the wearer's body, small fluid pumps circulate its contents through flexible pipes which run across the outer surface of the wearer's clothing. With adequately cool external conditions, the result is a surprisingly effective means of eliminating excess body heat, that doubles as a supply of clean drinking water.
sid_items_OXAGear_AutoClot_description: By utilising a combination of vasoactive medications and targeted electrostimulation, this device stems blood loss by causing damaged vessels to contract rapidly. Secondary medications supplement the clotting cascade and accelerate the healing process, as well as the user's metabolic rate.
sid_items_OXAGear_AutoHeal_description: An experimental system which reduces inflammation, accelerates coagulation, and promotes wound healing. Rumored to originate from the labs of SIRCAA, it bears resemblance to an extracorporeal membrane oxygenation device, augmented by an unknown artefact. The immediate benefits to combat personnel are obvious, but the long-term impact of such technology remains to be determined.
sid_items_OXAGear_AutoStim_description: The product of recently unearthed documents from the X-Lab network, revitalized by the renewed efforts of SIRCAA. Developed to augment combat personnel, this device accelerates audiovisual processing and neuronal response times, improving the reflexes and reaction times of the user. Despite its benefits, the device renders the operator particularly vulnerable to harmful psy radiation.
sid_items_OXAGear_HealthBoost_descriptio: A complex array of psy-emitters, potentiated by intravenously-administered neuroactive compounds, almost completely eliminates the users sense of pain. Rumoured to be the product of extensive reverse-engineering of Monolith technology procured by SIRCAA personnel.
sid_items_OXAGear_ReduceSleep_descriptio: The myriad threats of the zone are relentless; those that survive it must be even more so. This device was developed for extended operations into the heart of the zone, where a momentary lapse in concentration could spell disaster. Utilising an array of emissive electrodes adhered to the operator’s cranium, this device disrupts the natural circadian rhythm of the brain, effectively deceiving the body into a constant state of wakefulness. Whilst effective, users must remember that sleep is vital for the body, and prolonged use is medically questionable.
sid_items_OXAGear_RadFilter_description: A ruggedised medical device which counteracts the effects of harmful radiation. With SIRCAA personnel being constantly exposed to the hazards of the Zone, there is a strong desire within the organisation to develop an effective means of countering the constant threat of radiation poisoning. Whilst far from perfect, this device works by actively filtering the blood and administering automated doses of anti-radiation medication. Despite the benefits, the requirement for strong anticoagulant medications means it is a particularly risky option for combat personnel.
